<!-- begin fig-sp-diagram-pad -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/diagram-pad.svg
:label: fig-sp-diagram-pad
:class: col-body-outset-right

The window and the pad along $\tau$. Every transform runs over the window's $n$ slices, 4 free slots and 12 sponge slots together. The ramp carries light toward the head and into the free slots, the plane at the first of them is read into the bank each time the accumulated slippage crosses a whole slice, and the $\cos^2$ sponge falls to zero at the transform's periodic seam, so nothing comes round to the tail.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-diagram-pad -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-diagram-slippage -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/diagram-slippage.svg
:label: fig-sp-diagram-slippage
:class: col-body-outset-right

The slippage's two forms on a field of 4 slices a plane, under a step that slips one slice, a quarter of a plane. The ramp moves the field by the step's own slippage. The slice propagator's rotation moves the record by whole planes once 0.8 of a plane has accumulated, so its field would sit up to 0.8 of a plane behind the ramp's (shaded), which is why a field coarser than the beam's slices needs the ramp.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-diagram-slippage -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-diagram-planes -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/diagram-planes.svg
:label: fig-sp-diagram-planes
:class: col-body-outset-right

A field coarser than the beam's slices, here $m$ = 4 slices a plane. A beam slice sits between two planes and reads them by the linear weights $1 - w$ and $w$ along $\tau$ (left), so a slice on a plane reads that plane alone. The deposit splits the slice's source between the same two planes by the same weights divided by the $m$ slices a plane spans (right), so a uniform source over the slices gives every plane one slice's source, and the source filter runs once on each plane's sum.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-diagram-planes -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-vacuum -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/vacuum.svg
:label: fig-sp-vacuum
:class: col-body-outset-right

The vacuum test: the error of each propagator against the exact paraxial solution, from [](#tab-sp-vacuum). The slice propagator's error is 0.77 of the relative bandwidth at every row, the spatio-temporal coupling one $k_0$ cannot carry over two Rayleigh ranges, and the spectral propagator's is 1.1e-9 to 1.3e-8, the rounding of its transform pairs.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-vacuum -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-null -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/null.svg
:label: fig-sp-null
:class: col-body-outset-right

The null test: the SASE tier's power across the window at the exit under both propagators, with the source filter off (left) and on (right), from the runs of [](#tab-sp-null). With the filter off the two differ by 1.2e-1 of the exit power, 2.1e-1 of the bunching and 5.2e-1 of the energy, the wide-angle start-up light the frequency-dependent kernel delays. With it on they differ by 8.7e-3, 2.1e-3 and 6.0e-3.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-null -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-bank -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/bank.svg
:label: fig-sp-bank
:class: col-body-outset-right

The bank: the power in each plane of the pulse file the SASE tier's run leaves under both propagators, from [](#tab-sp-bank). Both bank 1216 planes. The pulse holds the window's energy plus the escaped energy to 1e-5 under the rotation and 6e-6 under the ramp, and the spectral run's pulse carries 8.5 percent more energy than the slice run's. The tail slice's share of the exit power is 2e-33 under the ramp.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-bank -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-cost -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/cost.svg
:label: fig-sp-cost
:class: col-body-outset-right

The cost: the field phase of a step of the SASE tier under both propagators, from [](#tab-sp-cost). The spectral propagator's field phase is 2.2 at 1 and 2.4 at 8 threads times the slice propagator's on this window of 32 planes with a pad of 16.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-cost -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-seeded -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/seeded.svg
:label: fig-sp-seeded
:class: col-body-outset-right

A chirped seed through the Aramis line under both propagators, with the source filter on, at each bandwidth of [](#tab-sp-seeded): the power across the window at the exit (top) and the exit spectrum about the carrier (bottom). Through the line the propagators differ by 1.6e-2 to 2.0e-2 of the peak field, 3.9e-4 to 4.7e-4 in wavelength and 0.4 percent to 0.7 percent in peak power. With the seed alone over the first segment they differ by 2.3e-3 to 6.5e-3 of the peak field after alignment, and with the beam's shot noise on by 6.5e-2 to 8.3e-2.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-seeded -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-chirped -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/chirped.svg
:label: fig-sp-chirped
:class: col-body-outset-right

An energy-chirped beam from noise through the Aramis line under both propagators, at each chirp of [](#tab-sp-chirped): the power across the window at the exit (top) and the exit spectrum about the carrier (bottom). The chirp decides the output: against the unchirped run's 4.15 µJ the pulse energy is 11.2 µJ, 995 nJ, 41.2 nJ at 0.25, 0.5, 1 percent. The two propagators agree on the fitted slope of the exit wavelengths to 3e-5, on the peak power to 2 percent and on the slice wavelengths to 1.6e-3, and their exit fields differ by 2.1e-2 to 6.7e-2 of the peak.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-chirped -->

<!-- begin fig-sp-sweep -->
:::{figure} generated/spectral/sweep.svg
:label: fig-sp-sweep
:class: col-body-outset-right

The sweep: the pulse energy at the exit (left) and the walk (right) against the field's plane as a fraction of the cooperation length, each over the same line's run at one plane a slice, from [](#tab-sp-sweep). The dotted line is the derived sampling, 0.1 of the cooperation length, and the dashed line the cliff at 0.25, above which a stated sampling is refused. A hollow point ran with the cliff raised. On the Aramis line of 1280 slices the pulse energy moves by 0.55 percent at 0.039, 1.3 percent at 0.097, 3.2 percent at 0.19, 11 percent at 0.39, 30 percent at 0.77 of the cooperation length, and the walk is 690, 501, 198, 148, 114, 96 s over the samplings.
:::
<!-- end fig-sp-sweep -->
